p: Woburn Safari Park is a full day out, so pace yourself. Many families like to do the road safari first while everyone's fresh and the car is cool, then park up for the foot safari, lunch and the play areas. If you fancy a second lap of the drive-through, check on the day whether that's allowed, as plans can change with the seasons. In hot weather keep plenty of water in the car, and in winter make sure the windows are clear so nobody misses a rhino through a steamy pane.

Animal talks are a highlight, so look at the day's schedule when you arrive and build lunch around the ones you don't want to miss. For little ones, a nap in the car during the road safari can work wonders for later, and grown-ups can enjoy watching the animals in peace for a bit.

There's plenty more nearby to fill a weekend. Bletchley Park, the home of the wartime codebreakers who cracked Enigma, is around twenty minutes' drive away near Milton Keynes. It's a fascinating, hands-on museum where older kids and adults can learn about Alan Turing and the secret world of codebreaking, and see the huts where it all happened.

If you're staying a few days, Center Parcs Woburn Forest is nearby for a woodland break, while Milton Keynes has plenty of shopping, parks and the Xscape centre with its indoor ski slope. For something calmer, the Greensand Ridge has lovely walks through heath and woodland across this part of Bedfordshire.
